description: Intent i012 (s02, optsize-body-clamp) complete. FINDING (high confidence): net/sched/sch_cake.c cake_get_tcpopt, lines 960-981 — the TCP-option walk does `opcode = *ptr++` then `opsize = *ptr++` with NO `if (length < 2)` guard between kind and size byte, exactly the seed (mptcp_get_options / 9609dad263f8) invariant violation. With length==1 it reads the opsize byte one past the option area; moreover its caller cake_get_tcphdr (lines 949-950) copies only min(__tcp_hdrlen, 64) bytes into a stack buffer (_tcph/_tcph_check, lines 1154-1155), so for doff>16 the walk driven by the full header length reads up to ~40 bytes past the 64-byte stack buffer (KASAN-detectable stack OOB read / uninitialized-stack info leak in the CAKE ack-filter path). The identical unguarded walk is duplicated in cake_tcph_may_drop, lines 1097-1141. Evidence: literal source quote verified present in the reported range; walk bounded by `opsize < 2 || opsize > length` only AFTER the unguarded size-byte read. Counterevidence checked — every other in-tree TCP option walker in s02 has the guard: net/ipv4/tcp_input.c tcp_parse_mss_option (line 3935), tcp_parse_options (line 3986, plus fastopen cookie memcpy clamped to 4..16 bytes, SMC read gated opsize>=6, EXP fastopen gated opsize>=4), tcp_parse_md5sig_option (loop precondition length>=18, lines 4138-4163), net/mptcp/options.c mptcp_get_options (line 359, seed already fixed there), net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_proto_tcp.c both walkers (lines 358, 420), net/netfilter/nf_synproxy_core.c (line 53) — all classified safe. Limitations: audit bounded to opsize/optlen-style option walkers in net/; wireless/Bluetooth IE and IP exthdr TLV branches out of scope (separate intents); impact for linear skbs with headroom may stay in-header, strongest over-read requires doff>16; no build/reproducer run (read-only tree), classification by direct source reading including skb_header_pointer (include/linux/skbuff.h 3681-3699) and skb_copy_bits (net/core/skbuff.c 2245-2263) semantics.
